review.intent_summary: Provide a versioned, independently pinnable Anomalyzer dependency that applications can install and run locally with its dependencies.

criteria.criterion: Wheel and source distributions carry the complete Python package, license, public API, CLI and read-only MCP entry points with one authoritative version.
Clean consumers outside the source checkout can install either distribution and exercise contracts, recipes, assessments, relationships, readiness and cases.
Version tags agree with package metadata and published release assets include SHA-256 checksums, source revision and pinned transitive dependencies.
A Linux Python 3.12 build bundles compatible binary dependencies and executes the consumer example with networking disabled.

verification_evidence: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest -q tests/test_release.py -p no:cacheprovider --basetemp <unique-user-profile-directory>: 16 passed on Python 3.12.9.
Inspected all implementation references and related public exports and MCP dispatch.
Reviewed docs/releases/README.md:239: adoption requires inspecting readiness and evidence limits; Guard retains severity, scheduling, persistence, incidents and notifications.
remaining_gaps: Fresh archive builds, inventory verification and clean wheel/sdist installation were not executed during this review.
The Linux Docker offline consumer check was inspected but not executed.
Published assets, remote tag identity, release immutability and successful release workflow runs were not independently checked.

issues.message: Capability or implementation changed during review. Run the review again.
